summary: Independent four-lens review of the S2 LangChain adapter spike, then adversarial verification of each finding

summaries.summary: Checked every outcome path against docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md, interfaces.py, toolbox.py and worker.py, reading the installed langgraph/langchain source and running read-only in-memory probes (no files written, run_spike.py not run). Sound: BudgetExceeded and ReplayMiss leave graph.invoke with their original types (ToolNode's default handler only converts ToolInvocationError), and even when an outer ToolRetryMiddleware swallows them into a ToolMessage the ToolBox latches still fire, so FAIL/budget and ERROR/replay_miss hold; non-JSON arguments as FAIL/crash and non-JSON or Command results as ERROR/harness_error match AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:112-116; before_model gives one budgeted model_step per model call; replay does run the real graph in the child against the recording, with the limit FINDINGS already states (the graded final_output comes from the sealed snapshot, hosted model calls are not replayed). Minor only: the extra note_model_step('adapter rejected tool result') at adapter_spike.py:162 is a diagnostic, not a policy step, and spends model-step budget.

Read the installed langchain 1.4.9 factory.py and middleware/types.py and langgraph tool_node.py, and ran small in-memory probes (no files written, run_spike.py not run). Sound: wrap_tool_call is a public, documented AgentMiddleware hook and short-circuiting without the handler is documented and used by LangChain's own middleware, so the stability claim is fair; raising in after_model does prevent every tool execution; BudgetExceeded/ReplayMiss propagate through create_agent's default ToolNode handler and are latched by the worker regardless; unknown tools reach the middleware with request.tool None and get ToolBox's unknown_tool fault; the skipped schema validation and injected arguments are already disclosed in FINDINGS. Not sound as written: fault delivery, the multi-call policy, and message shapes, per the three findings.

Checked the recommended product API against the plan's entry-cost goal and against worker.py, toolbox.py, interfaces.py, replay.py, contracts.py and the installed LangChain 1.4.9 source, including in-memory probes of the lighter design in record and replay modes. The spike's mechanics are sound (exactly-once through ToolBox, faults fire, budget and replay semantics, snapshot-carried final answer, process-local binding), and no frozen interface blocks deriving the toolset from the user's BaseTools; the only forced glue is three module-level refs and seed-independent tool schemas for replay. The product should adopt the derived design and let faults surface as exceptions, not the API as written in FINDINGS.md.

I checked each of the nine checks in run_spike.py against the run-0004 files and the ARCI and LangChain sources. Sound: fault accounting is read from recorded tool_finish.injected_by events (4 per condition, matching trials.jsonl), budget ends FAIL/budget with one tool_start, the snapshot ablation isolates the captured answer, replay ran on a failing candidate trial using the bundle-embedded source and consumed its one recorded call, the diff output (common_prefix 5, tool_start versus agent_result after tool_timeout) matches the events, the parallel probe uses a barrier rather than timing, and every number in FINDINGS.md and CODEX_REPORT.md matches the recorded files (verdicts are identical across runs 0003, 0004 and 0005). The exactly-once count only observes the ToolBox-side body, but the handler is discarded by construction and the schema-only tripwire would propagate under LangChain's default error handling, so I did not report it; the Command/set rejection message lives only in the snapshot and a model_step event, which FINDINGS already discloses.

surviving.title: Faults are delivered as adapter-built error ToolMessages, bypassing LangChain's own error path, so the gate measures an agent that does not exist in production
surviving.claim: The adapter catches every ToolFault inside its own wrap_tool_call and returns ToolMessage(status="error"). In installed LangChain 1.4.9 a create_agent tool exception is NOT turned into a ToolMessage by default; it propagates out of invoke, and the idiomatic recovery (ToolRetryMiddleware / ToolErrorMiddleware) keys off an exception from the handler. Result: an agent with no error handling is credited with model-level recovery it would not have when deployed (false PASS), and a candidate hardened with ToolRetryMiddleware gets no credit because the retry middleware never sees an exception (false FAIL). FINDINGS Q2 ('a real tool exception has the same message behavior') only compares the adapter with itself, not with native LangChain.
surviving.evidence: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:164-170 converts ToolFault to an error ToolMessage; FINDINGS.md:41, :64 and :90 recommend this for the product. Native behaviour: /Users/ajay/Developer/.arci-worktrees/v2-spike-venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py:391-399 (_default_handle_tool_errors re-raises everything except ToolInvocationError) and langchain/agents/factory.py:1141-1145 (create_agent builds ToolNode with that default, no user override); langchain/agents/middleware/tool_error.py:38-45 states conversion is opt-in, otherwise the exception halts the run; langchain/agents/middleware/tool_retry.py:323-347 retries only on an exception from handler. Read-only in-memory probes (nothing written): (A) native create_agent(ScriptedModel(retry=True), raising-once tool) -> invoke raised RuntimeError('fixture service unavailable'), whereas the same agent under the adapter is PASS in out/run-0004/real-error-baseline.trial.json (run_spike.py:210-228). (B) native ToolRetryMiddleware + non-retrying model + raising-once tool -> final 'forty-two', 2 body calls; same middleware list plus BoundaryMiddleware over a real ToolBox with tool_error_once -> final 'unavailable', toolbox.tool_calls == 1, in either middleware order. The task brief itself (tasks/S2-langchain-adapter-spike.md, question 2) asserts the ToolMessage premise, so the spike inherited it rather than checked it.
surviving.recommendation: In the product adapter let ToolFault leave the innermost wrap_tool_call as an exception (ArciMiddleware last in the list, ToolBox call in the handler position), so the user's ToolRetryMiddleware / ToolErrorMiddleware and ToolNode's default behave as deployed; an unhandled fault then ends as uncaught ToolFault = FAIL/crash, which is exactly the rule in docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:8-9 and interfaces.py:50-51. If message conversion is offered at all, make it an explicit opt-in that the report states. Add an offline test for both directions (no handling -> FAIL; ToolRetryMiddleware -> second ToolBox call, PASS) before phase 3 and before the phase 5 study design relies on 'models recover from tool faults'.

verification.reasoning:
I tried to refute this by reading the cited code and re-running the probes in memory (nothing written); every load-bearing part held.

**What the adapter does**
- `/Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:164-170` catches `ToolFault` inside `wrap_tool_call` and returns `ToolMessage(status="error")`; line 147 discards `handler`.
- `FINDINGS.md:41`, `:64` ("The middleware directly calls ToolBox and constructs ToolMessages") and `:90` ("failures use error status") carry this into the product recommendation.

**What installed LangChain does natively**
- `langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py:391-399`: `_default_handle_tool_errors` returns a message only for `ToolInvocationError` and re-raises everything else.
- `tool_node.py:1019-1023` and `:1076-1082`: both the direct path and the wrapper path route through that default, so an ordinary exception propagates.
- `langchain/agents/factory.py:1141-1145`: `create_agent` builds `ToolNode(tools=..., wrap_tool_call=..., awrap_tool_call=...)` with no `handle_tool_errors` override.
- `langchain/agents/middleware/tool_error.py:38-45`: conversion to an error message is opt-in; otherwise the exception propagates, "halting the run".
- `langchain/agents/middleware/tool_retry.py:322-350`: the retry loop triggers only on an exception raised by `handler(request)`.

**Probes I ran myself**

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Native `create_agent`, raising-once tool, no middleware, `ScriptedModel(retry=True)` | `invoke` raised `RuntimeError('fixture service unavailable')`, 1 body call (same with `retry=False`) |
| Same agent under the adapter (`out/run-0004/real-error-baseline.trial.json`) | PASS, 2 tool calls |
| Native `ToolRetryMiddleware` + non-retrying model + raising-once tool | final `'forty-two'`, 2 body calls |
| `ToolRetryMiddleware` + `BoundaryMiddleware` over a real `ToolBox` with `tool_error_once`, both orders | final `'unavailable'`, `toolbox.tool_calls == 1`, 0 body calls |
| Recommended design: innermost middleware lets `ToolFault` propagate, no handling | `invoke` raises `ToolFault` |
| Recommended design with `ToolRetryMiddleware` outer and non-retrying model | 2 ToolBox calls, final `'forty-two'` |

- An uncaught `ToolFault` maps to FAIL/crash at `src/arci/worker.py:165-167`, matching `docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:8-9` and `src/arci/interfaces.py:47-52`.
- `factory.py:713` confirms the first middleware is outermost, so "ArciMiddleware last" is the correct placement.

**The Q2 claim in FINDINGS**
- `run_spike.py:210-228` (`real_error`) only runs `adapter_spike:baseline/candidate` through the runner.
- The real `RuntimeError` is caught by `ToolBox.__execute` (`src/arci/toolbox.py:296-306`), re-raised as `ToolFault`, and converted by the adapter. No native LangChain control exists, so "a real tool exception has the same message behavior" compares the adapter with itself.
- The brief (`tasks/S2-langchain-adapter-spike.md:67-69`) asserts the ToolMessage premise, so the spike inherited it.

**Caveats that narrow but do not refute**
- `FINDINGS.md:94` and `:134-136` flag in general terms that bypassing the handler bypasses "handler middleware" and that composition "must be rejected or separately proven". Neither says the native default is to raise, nor that an outer `ToolRetryMiddleware` is silently neutralised.
- "An agent that does not exist in production" is too strong for two cases: agents with a catch-all `ToolErrorMiddleware`, and agents whose tools return error strings themselves. For those, message conversion approximates deployed behaviour, with different content.
- The gate is baseline-versus-candidate, so the bias changes a verdict mainly when the two arms differ in exception-level handling, for example a candidate that adds or removes `ToolRetryMiddleware`. That is the motivating use case, so the "changes-design" severity stands.

surviving.title: Adapter limitations triggered by legal model behaviour are scored as agent FAIL/crash and count against the arm
surviving.claim: When the model emits two tool calls in one message, or a final message whose content is a list of blocks, or the user invokes async, the adapter raises a plain ValueError and the worker records FAIL/crash, which the gate counts as an arm failure. These are things the adapter does not support, not agent failures; ARCI's own frozen precedent for boundary-unsupported concurrency is harness_error (ERROR, experiment invalid). With hosted models that issue parallel tool calls or block-list content at different rates (the phase 5 study compares two hosted models), a candidate can be BLOCKed purely by the adapter.
surviving.evidence: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:125-129 (multi-call ValueError in after_model), :131-136 (final content must be str), :138-140 and :184-190 (async). Evidence envelopes: out/run-0004/parallel.trial.json and unsupported-async.trial.json both outcome FAIL, termination crash (asserted as expected at run_spike.py:331 and :352). Worker maps any agent-side exception to CRASH: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/worker.py:168-171; the only harness latch is ToolBox's private __mark_harness (src/arci/toolbox.py:154-156), unreachable through ToolBoxProtocol (src/arci/interfaces.py:79-92), so the spike had no way to produce ERROR. Precedent: docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:189-192 ('a second tools/call while one is in flight latches harness_error') and :329-331 ('concurrent decision requests are unsupported' = harness fault); :222-227 reserve 'agent's problem' for agent protocol mistakes; :58 gate counts only PASS as success; :280 any trial ERROR makes the decision ERROR. Probe: a fake model returning AIMessage(content=[{'type':'text','text':'forty-two'}]) under BoundaryMiddleware raised 'ValueError: S2: final output must be a text AIMessage' although the answer is correct; langchain_core/messages/base.py:263 provides message.text for list content. Fan-out is one Send per call (langchain/agents/factory.py:2032), so after_model runs single-threaded before it. FINDINGS.md:46-47 and :91-92 report FAIL/crash without discussing attribution.
surviving.recommendation: Decide attribution before phase 3: (1) capture final output with message.text so block-list content is not a crash; (2) for multi-call messages either support them with a deterministic serial order (for example a turnstile keyed on the call's index in the AIMessage, or pre-executing in after_model in message order; neither was tried in the spike, and FINDINGS.md:91 only rules out a plain mutex) or report them as ERROR/harness_error with a fixed detail, which needs a small harness-owned 'unsupported' channel on ToolBox (toolbox.py and worker.py are not in FROZEN.sha256; the frozen ToolBoxProtocol would need an additive method or the adapter must type against ToolBox); (3) never let an adapter refusal count as a FAIL in the gate, and state in the recipe that ERROR here means 'could not measure'.

I re-read every cited location and ran two in-memory probes (no files written). The core of the finding survives; two sub-claims do not.

CONFIRMED
- Adapter refusals are plain ValueError: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:125-129 (multi-call), :131-136 (final content must be str), :138-140 and :184-190 (async).
- Worker turns any agent-side exception into CRASH: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/worker.py:168-171. Runner maps CRASH to Outcome.FAIL: src/arci/runner.py:206-208. Gate counts only PASS as success: src/arci/gate.py:56; any trial ERROR makes the decision ERROR: gate.py:320 and docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:280.
- Evidence envelopes: out/run-0004/parallel.trial.json and unsupported-async.trial.json are both outcome FAIL, termination crash, tool_calls 0; asserted as expected at run_spike.py:331 and :352.
- Precedent quoted accurately: docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:189-192 (second tools/call in flight latches harness_error), :329-331 (concurrent decisions are a harness fault), :222-227 (agent protocol mistakes are the agent's problem), :58 (success = PASS). These are command/MCP-path rules, so they are an analogy for the Python path, not a binding rule.
- Probe reproduced: under BoundaryMiddleware, a fake model returning AIMessage(content=[{'type':'text','text':'forty-two'}]) raised 'ValueError: S2: final output must be a text AIMessage' with final_output None, while message.text == 'forty-two' (langchain_core/messages/base.py:262-292). The check only bites on the FINAL message: list content on an intermediate tool-calling message ran fine.
- Fan-out is one Send per pending call (langchain/agents/factory.py:2032); the two-call probe raised in after_model with zero ToolBox calls.
- FINDINGS.md:46-47 and :91-92 report FAIL/crash with no discussion of attribution. The brief (tasks/S2-langchain-adapter-spike.md:79-83) and PLAN.md:191-193 ask only for a 'clear error' and leave attribution open. toolbox.py and worker.py are not in FROZEN.sha256; interfaces.py is.

NOT SUPPORTED
1. 'The spike had no way to produce ERROR' is false. worker.py:183-189 calls toolset.snapshot() inside the outer try, and any exception there latches harness_error. I ran arci.worker.main() in memory on out/run-0004/parallel.spec.json with World.snapshot patched to raise when the adapter had recorded a refusal: the result was a harness_error latch and termination harness_error, detail 'RuntimeError: adapter could not measure: unsupported: S<n>: parallel tool calls unsupported...'. So ERROR attribution is reachable with unchanged src and the unchanged frozen ToolBoxProtocol. Limit: replay mode never calls snapshot (worker.py:180-181), so a replayed refusal would still surface as FAIL/crash; a first-class channel is cleaner but not required.
2. Async is not 'legal model behaviour'. It is the agent author's choice of ainvoke, it fails every trial of that arm deterministically, and FAIL/crash for an agent function that raises matches ARCI's Python-path rule. It does not create a model-dependent differential.

NOT VERIFIABLE HERE
- That hosted models differ in parallel-call or block-list rates: no provider package is installed in the spike venv (only langchain, langchain_core, langchain_protocol), so this is plausible but unevidenced. Providers generally let parallel tool calls be disabled, which FINDINGS.md never tells the user to do (the error text only says 'request one call per message').

ADDITION
- The bias is two-sided: if the baseline model trips the adapter more often than the candidate, the baseline's FAILs inflate and a non-inferiority gate can falsely PASS, not only falsely BLOCK.
verification.corrected_claim: When the model emits more than one tool call in a message, or a final AIMessage whose content is a list of blocks, the spike adapter raises a plain ValueError (adapter_spike.py:125-136); the worker records FAIL/crash (worker.py:168-171, runner.py:206-208) and the gate counts it as a non-success for that arm (gate.py:56). These are adapter limitations, not agent failures, and they can bias the gate in either direction (false BLOCK or false PASS) if the two arms trigger them at different rates; FINDINGS.md:46-47 and :91-92 adopt FAIL/crash without discussing attribution, and ARCI's command-path precedent for unsupported concurrency is harness_error (AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:189-192, :329-331). The final-text crash is avoidable by capturing message.text. Async invocation is a user-code choice, not model behaviour; it fails every trial deterministically and FAIL/crash is consistent with existing Python-path semantics. Contrary to the finding, ERROR/harness_error is already reachable with unchanged src and the unchanged frozen protocol: a toolset snapshot() that raises when the adapter recorded a refusal latches harness_error (worker.py:183-189, verified in memory), though not in replay mode, so a dedicated ToolBox channel is an optional refinement rather than a prerequisite. Phase 3 should decide the attribution explicitly, and the recipe should tell users to disable parallel tool calls at the provider.

surviving.title: Real tool error text is scrubbed by the kernel before the model sees it, and FINDINGS presents the path as faithful
surviving.claim: For a tool that really raises, ToolBox stores error_detail through format_diagnostic, which keeps only the first line and replaces numbers, paths and hex with placeholders; the adapter forwards that string as the ToolMessage content. An LLM agent therefore recovers from 'order <n> not found in <path>; retry after <n> seconds' instead of the real message, and any resulting failure is recorded as an agent FAIL. The spike's fixture message contains no digits or paths, so its 'real tool exception' evidence does not exercise this.
surviving.evidence: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/toolbox.py:300-307 (error_detail=format_diagnostic(exc)) and :23-41 (format_diagnostic returns normalise(text)); /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/fingerprint.py:16-25 (first line only; _PATH, _HEX, _NUM substituted). Adapter forwards it verbatim: plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:165-166. Read-only probe with a real ToolBox and a tool raising RuntimeError('order 4411 not found in /var/data/orders/eu-west; retry after 30 seconds\nsecond line hint') produced the observation {'status': 'error', 'content': 'error: RuntimeError: order <n> not found in <path>; retry after <n> seconds'}. The spike's only real-error fixture is 'fixture service unavailable' (adapter_spike.py:79; out/run-0004/real-error-baseline.trial.json:183), and FINDINGS.md:41 concludes 'A real tool exception has the same message behavior'. The scrubbing is deliberate for sealed text (docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:249-251) but was designed for code agents that branch on kind, not for a model reading the text.
surviving.recommendation: Record this as an explicit limit or design decision for the adapter: either document in docs/recipes/langchain.md that tools under ARCI must report recoverable errors as returned JSON values (raised exceptions reach the model scrubbed and single-line), or decide in an ADR whether the agent-visible detail may differ from the sealed, normalised one (which also has to hold in REPLAY, where only the recorded detail exists). Add a fixture with digits and a path to the adapter's unit tests so the behaviour is pinned either way, and correct the FINDINGS Q2 wording.

verification.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it; the framing around it is overstated in three places.

**Confirmed**
- `/Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/toolbox.py:298-307`: a raising tool becomes `ToolResult(ok=False, error_kind="error", error_detail=format_diagnostic(exc))`. Line 255 re-raises it to the agent as `ToolFault(result.error_kind, result.error_detail)`, so the scrubbed string is the only text the agent can get.
- `toolbox.py:23-41`: `format_diagnostic` returns `normalise(text)`.
- `/Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/src/arci/fingerprint.py:17-25`: `normalise` keeps the first line only, then substitutes `_PATH`, `_HEX` and `_NUM` (non-strict is the default).
- `/Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:164-170`: the adapter forwards `f"{exc.kind}: {exc.detail}"` as the `ToolMessage` content.
- My own read-only probe (real `ToolBox`, the spike's `BoundaryMiddleware.wrap_tool_call`, a tool raising the reviewer's two-line message) returned content `'error: RuntimeError: order <n> not found in <path>; retry after <n> seconds'` with status `error`. The second line was dropped.
- Two further probes: an ISO-date message became `'ValueError: date must be after <n>-<n>-<n>, got <n>-<n>-<n>; max <n> items'`, and `KeyError('SKU-00012345')` became `"KeyError: 'SKU-<hex>'"`.
- The spike's only real-exception fixture is `RuntimeError("fixture service unavailable")` (`adapter_spike.py:79`), with no digits, path or second line. The verifier only checks that substring (`run_spike.py:221`), and the evidence shows it passing through unchanged (`out/run-0004/real-error-baseline.trial.json:183`). The spike therefore never exercises the scrubbing.
- Nothing in `FINDINGS.md`, including the risks at lines 126-142 and the supported-subset row at line 90, mentions that raised error text is normalised.

**Overstated or wrong**
1. "FINDINGS presents the path as faithful" is too strong. `FINDINGS.md:41` says only "A real tool exception has the same message behavior", in a sentence about faults becoming `ToolMessage(status="error")`. That is literally true and supported. The defect is an undisclosed limit, not a false fidelity claim.
2. `docs/AGENT_SEMANTICS.md:249-251` is the rule for the MCP bridge (`arci.mcp_toolset_server`), not the in-process `ToolBox`. The frozen rule covering the toolbox helper is lines 145-148, which requires one line, never raising and UTF-8 safety, but does not require number or path scrubbing.
3. "Designed for code agents that branch on kind" is unsupported by anything I found.

**Context that lowers the weight**
- This is existing v1.0.0 kernel behaviour for every Python agent, not something the adapter introduces.
- It applies identically to the baseline and candidate arms, so it does not bias the gate. The cost is fidelity: the agent under test sees less informative error text than in production, and a failure caused by that is recorded as an agent FAIL.
- `toolbox.py` is not in the frozen list in `AGENTS.md`, and I found no acceptance test pinning scrubbed tool error detail (grep of `tests/acceptance` for `error_detail` and `normalise` returned nothing). Showing the model different text from the sealed text is therefore an open ADR choice rather than a frozen-contract conflict, though replay only has the recorded detail.

The recommendation (document the limit or decide it in an ADR, pin with a digits-and-path fixture, tighten the Q2 wording) stands. "Changes-design" fits only if the ADR chooses to split agent-visible from sealed detail; otherwise it is a documented limit plus one test.
verification.corrected_claim:
For a tool that really raises, the v1 ToolBox (src/arci/toolbox.py:298-307, raised to the agent at :255) gives the agent only format_diagnostic(exc): the first line, with paths, hex runs and all numbers replaced by placeholders (src/arci/fingerprint.py:17-25). The spike adapter forwards that string as the ToolMessage content (adapter_spike.py:164-170). An LLM agent therefore sees e.g. 'error: RuntimeError: order <n> not found in <path>; retry after <n> seconds' and loses any later lines.

This is existing kernel behaviour for all Python agents, not adapter-specific, and it affects both arms equally. It does not bias the gate, but it makes the tested environment less informative than production, and failures it causes are scored as agent FAILs.

FINDINGS.md does not claim text fidelity. Line 41 ('A real tool exception has the same message behavior') is true as a statement about status="error" delivery. What is missing is any disclosure of the limit: the spike's only real-error fixture ('fixture service unavailable', adapter_spike.py:79, checked by substring at run_spike.py:221) has no digits, paths or second line, so it cannot reveal the scrubbing.

The number and path scrubbing rule at :249-251 is for the MCP bridge. The product adapter should document that recoverable errors must be returned as JSON values, or take that ADR decision, and pin the behaviour with a digits-and-path fixture.

surviving.title: Injected faults are converted to ToolMessages inside the middleware, which is not how LangChain 1.4.9 surfaces real tool failures and disables the agent's own retry/error middleware in either list position
surviving.claim: In native create_agent a tool exception is not shown to the model by default: ToolNode's default handler re-raises everything except argument-validation errors, so the run crashes unless the user adds ToolRetryMiddleware/ToolErrorMiddleware. The spike catches ToolFault and returns ToolMessage(status="error") itself, so an agent with no error handling looks recoverable under ARCI while it would crash in production, and an agent that does use ToolRetryMiddleware never gets its retries exercised (outermost: its hook is skipped; innermost: it sees a normal return, not an exception). FINDINGS Q2 ("a real tool exception has the same message behavior") only compares injected vs real faults inside the adapter, never against native LangChain.
surviving.evidence: Native path: /Users/ajay/Developer/.arci-worktrees/v2-spike-venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/langgraph/prebuilt/tool_node.py:391-399 (_default_handle_tool_errors returns only ToolInvocationError, else `raise e`), :997-1029 and :1071-1088 (applied to tool body and to wrapper exceptions); langchain/agents/factory.py:1140-1145 builds ToolNode with no handle_tool_errors override; langchain/agents/middleware/types.py:685 documents 'Exceptions propagate'. Retry path: langchain/agents/middleware/tool_retry.py:323-353 retries only on exceptions raised by handler(request); composition is first=outermost (factory.py:710-755). Spike: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/plan/exec/v2/spikes/s2/adapter_spike.py:147 (del handler) and :164-170 (ToolFault -> ToolMessage). Claim: FINDINGS.md:41, :64-65; check that backs it is adapter-only: run_spike.py:210-228. Read-only in-memory probes I ran against the installed packages: (1) create_agent with a tool raising RuntimeError and no middleware -> invoke RAISED RuntimeError after 1 body call; (2) same tool + ToolRetryMiddleware, model that never retries -> final 'forty-two', 2 body calls; (3) spike BoundaryMiddleware + ToolRetryMiddleware with a ToolBox stub faulting once -> final 'unavailable', 1 ToolBox call, in BOTH orders [Boundary, Retry] and [Retry, Boundary]; (4) BudgetExceeded raised under an outer ToolRetryMiddleware is retried 3 times and returned to the model as an error ToolMessage (outcome is still protected by the worker latch, src/arci/worker.py:191-199, but the run continues). surviving.recommendation: Make the product middleware the innermost wrap_tool_call (last in the middleware list, enforced or documented) and have it re-raise the ToolFault as an exception in place of the tool body, so LangChain's outer middleware stack and ToolNode error policy treat an injected fault exactly as they treat a real one; each retry then becomes a second recorded, budgeted ToolBox.call. Do not build the error ToolMessage in the adapter. Add an offline test with ToolRetryMiddleware and one with no error middleware, each compared against the same agent run natively. In LangChain 1.4.9 a tool exception propagates out of invoke by default, and robustness is added with ToolRetryMiddleware or ToolErrorMiddleware, which act on exceptions from the handler. The spike's middleware returns a message instead of raising, so those middlewares never fire: an agent that natively survives a transient error is reported as failing, and a candidate that removes its retry middleware looks identical to its baseline.

surviving.recommendation: In the product adapter, raise injected and real tool failures as exceptions from the tool-execution position and require the ARCI middleware to be the last (innermost) entry, so the user's own ToolRetryMiddleware, ToolErrorMiddleware or absence of either decides the outcome. Each retry then passes through ToolBox again and is recorded and budgeted. If a convert-to-message mode is kept, make it an explicit opt-in named in the report. Add a native-versus-adapter parity test for a raising tool to the phase 3 acceptance, and correct the wording at FINDINGS.md:41 and the brief's assumption (S2 task lines 67-70) before the adapter is specified from them.

The figures are load-sensitive: run-0005, same source, shows 1.40 s import and about 2.86 s per trial. The right planning number is about 1.5 s per graded trial on a quiet machine, beside a no-LangChain control of about 0.2 s per process. Phase 3 should have the scaffold keep the oracle in a module that does not import LangChain and report wall_seconds from real envelopes.
